atoms.text: As the greenhouse effect increases global temperatures, the oceans have been getting warmer, and glaciers have started melting. This has resulted in rising sea levels, which have caused flooding in many parts of the world.

Additionally, warmer ocean temperatures lead to extreme weather events. If the ocean temperature is above 27 °C, hurricanes and typhoons are able to form. These can be devastating for the people affected, as well as the surrounding ecosystems and landscapes that get destroyed.
Forest fires have also started becoming more frequent due to higher temperatures, as well as less rainfall and moisture. This only makes climate change worse by destroying our forests.

atoms.a: Which of the following are caused by the greenhouse effect?
What can form if the ocean gets hotter than 27 °C?
Why are forest fires bad for the environment?

atoms.a: Higher temperatures and rising sea levels are causing stronger, more frequent storms and flooding.
The number of wildfires occurring in the UK each year keeps going up, polluting the air and destroying animal habitats.
More heatwaves are happening each year in the UK, and temperatures are reaching record highs.
Sea levels are rising and storms are wearing down British coastlines.
Select the purple area on the map of Southern Africa.

feedback.end: In March 2019, the area shown on the map was hit by Cyclone Idai.

atoms.b: Forming in the ((++Indian Arctic)) Ocean and spreading across parts of Mozambique, Zimbabwe, Malawi and ((++Madagascar Sweden)), Cyclone Idai was incredibly deadly and killed over 1,500 people.
Higher global temperatures will result in ((++oceans sees)) reaching 27 °C more often, which means that similar ((++cyclones earthquakes)) will become more common.
